title: TLS Handshake
body:
Once the [[TCP Three-Way Handshake]] has opened a raw connection, TLS negotiates encryption over it. The server presents its certificate, the client validates that certificate against a chain of trust ending at a [[Certificate Authority]] it already trusts, and the two sides agree on session keys used to encrypt everything that follows. In the postal analogy: both sides agree on a secret code so nobody along the route can read the letter.

This is negotiated between your browser's networking/crypto layer and the server's TLS termination point — which is often the [[Load Balancer]] or a CDN edge, not the application server itself. Only after the handshake completes does the first HTTP request byte get sent. Everything TLS provides is described in [[HTTPS]].
